claims.text: Corrosion resistance in stainless steels for chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications is primarily governed by preferential chromium segregation to grain boundaries and the near-surface region.
Chromium segregation produces a continuous Cr2O3 passive layer.
The Cr2O3 passive layer is self-healing and blocks aggressive ions.
Moderate heating and irradiation enhance chromium diffusion without degrading the protective film.
The proposed initial material is a conventional stainless steel such as an 18Cr-8Ni grade with an initially uniform bulk composition.
Controlled pre-oxidation or low-dose irradiation can stimulate chromium segregation without causing bulk degradation.
Nanometer-scale chromium-enriched layers at grain boundaries and near the surface promote rapid formation and regeneration of a continuous Cr2O3 film.
Chromium diffuses preferentially along grain boundaries and toward the steel surface under corrosive, thermal, and moderate-irradiation conditions.
Localized chromium enrichment facilitates rapid nucleation and growth of a protective Cr2O3 film.
Regeneration of the chromium oxide film after local disruption impedes ingress of corrosive species.
Refractory high-entropy alloys have shown resistance to irradiation damage.
Grain-boundary segregation and regulated phase formation are responsible for enhanced external-damage resistance in the cited high-entropy and refractory alloys.
Chromium-segregation-enhanced samples will exhibit lower electrochemical corrosion current density than untreated samples.
Chromium-segregation-enhanced samples will exhibit lower pit density than untreated samples.
Chromium-segregation-enhanced samples will form more uniform and continuous passive films than untreated samples.
The proposed mechanism should operate only below temperatures that destabilize the protective film.
The proposed mechanism should apply at chloride levels typical of chemical-processing streams.
Approximately 11-12 wt% chromium is the critical minimum chromium content needed for passivity.
